## Samsung reportedly achieves 80% 'golden yield' on HBM4, challenging SK Hynix's AI memory leadership

HBM4 yield parity would erode SK Hynix's pricing power and give hyperscalers — and NVIDIA — a credible second-source option, with potential margin and supply-security implications for the entire AI memory stack.

- Samsung is reported to have reached an 80% yield rate on HBM4, described in the headline as the 'golden yield' threshold.
- The achievement is framed as Samsung's bid to challenge SK Hynix's dominant position in AI DRAM.
- Coverage is single-outlet and the yield figure is attributed as 'reportedly,' carrying a verification caveat.
- If confirmed, this would represent a meaningful competitive inflection for Samsung in the high-margin HBM segment.
